title: Which DJI drones can live stream? Model and controller list (2026)
description: Every DJI drone that can live stream in DJI Fly, from Mini 2 and Mini 4K to Mavic 4 Pro and Avata 360, which controllers work, and the 720p and microphone limits.
h1: Which DJI drones can live stream? The full model and controller list
lead: DJI lists livestreaming in DJI Fly for the Mini series (Mavic Mini to Mini 5 Pro, including Mini 4K and Mini 2 SE), the Air series (Mavic Air 2 to Air 3S), Mavic 3 and Mavic 4 Pro, Neo and Neo 2, Flip, Avata, Avata 2, Avata 360, DJI FPV and Lito. What decides it in practice is the controller: the original DJI RC cannot stream, and the RC 2 streams only 720p.
summary: DJI Fly has had livestreaming since version 1.4.12. DJI’s own guide lists 26 drones across the Mini, Air, Mavic, Neo, Flip, Avata, FPV and Lito series.
Phone controllers (RC-N1, RC-N2, RC-N3) stream RTMP at 1080p or 720p; the bitrate is 5 or 3 Mbps on Android and 2 or 1 Mbps on iOS.
The DJI RC 2 and RC Pro 2 stream only 720p because of their hardware; the RC Pro streams only 720p after DJI Fly 1.18.0.
The original DJI RC does not support livestreaming. The RC 2, RC Pro and Smart Controller need a microphone from DJI Fly 1.16.0.
Avata 360 streams the normal transmission view only, not 360° mode. Goggles stream through a phone running DJI Fly.

blocks.p: The controller matters more than the drone. A Mini 3 Pro or Mavic 3 sold with the screen DJI RC can fly but not stream; the same drone on an RC-N1 with a phone streams. The 720p limit applies to the live picture only: the video recorded on the drone keeps its full resolution.

sections.h2: How to check your own drone

steps.t: Update DJI Fly and the firmware
steps.d: Livestreaming needs DJI Fly 1.4.12 or newer, and newer drones get it with later versions. Update the app, the controller and the aircraft.
Turn both on and wait until DJI Fly shows GO FLY. A phone controller must be connected to the phone by cable.
Tap GO FLY → ••• → Transmission → Live Streaming Platforms. If RTMP is listed, your combination can stream.
Enter the address Stream My Drone shows on a phone or computer and tap Start Livestream. The picture with its real resolution and bitrate appears in the app within seconds.

sections.h2: Drones and cameras outside DJI Fly

list: Older DJI GO 4 drones (Mavic 2, Mavic Pro, Phantom 4): DJI GO 4 has its own livestream menu with a custom RTMP option.
Enterprise drones (Matrice, Mavic 3 Enterprise): they stream from DJI Pilot 2 on the RC Plus; that workflow is not covered here.
Osmo cameras (Pocket 3, Action): they stream from DJI Mimo; see the Pocket 3 and Osmo Action guides.

blocks.p: Aircraft list, controller notes, Avata 360 and goggles notes: DJI Fly livestream guide (Chinese). Version, resolution, bitrate and microphone requirements: DJI Fly App Livestream Operation Guides. Checked on November 8, 2026.

faq.q: Can the DJI Mini 4K live stream?
faq.a: Yes. DJI lists the Mini 4K among the drones with livestreaming in DJI Fly. It uses a phone controller, so you can choose 1080p or 720p in DJI Fly.

faq.q: Can the DJI Mini 2 SE and Mini 2 live stream?
faq.a: Yes. Both are on DJI’s list, as are the Mini SE and the original Mavic Mini. Update DJI Fly first; livestreaming needs version 1.4.12 or newer.

faq.q: Why can’t my DJI RC live stream?
faq.a: DJI states that livestreaming is not supported with the original DJI RC. Use the same drone with an RC-N1, RC-N2 or RC-N3 and a phone, or with a DJI RC 2 if the drone supports it.

faq.q: Why does the DJI RC 2 stream only 720p?
faq.a: DJI says the RC 2 and RC Pro 2 support only 720p livestreaming because of their hardware. The recording on the drone is not affected.
No. DJI states that the Avata 360 does not support livestreaming in 360° mode; it streams the normal video transmission view.

faq.q: Can the DJI Air 2S live stream?
faq.a: Yes. The Air 2S and the Mavic Air 2 are on DJI’s list of drones with livestreaming in DJI Fly, through the RTMP option.
